dossiers.catalyst_stack: Tesla converted autonomy from promise to product: Dutch FSD Supervised type approval on April 10, 2026, a Nevada permit for up to 5,000 robotaxis on August 20, and paid Austin Cybercab rides from September 4. Volume prints stayed constructive, with record Q2 deliveries of 480,126 on July 2 and a Q3 beat at 486,532 on October 2, plus a Q1 earnings beat on April 22. Fundamentals cracked on July 22 when Q2 non-GAAP EPS of $0.33 missed and free cash flow went about $1.1 billion negative, after which Tesla lined up $30 billion of credit on September 29. Safety and regulatory overhangs rose with a July 29 NHTSA probe covering about 1.2 million vehicles and a September 3 Cybercab FMVSS audit, while the Street split into October 8 between UBS at $391 and JPMorgan’s cut to $415.
dossiers.key_assumption: The Cybercab NHTSA audit remains an inquiry rather than a service halt or FMVSS block, and Q3 results do not extend Q2’s margin and free-cash-flow miss.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On April 16, 2026 Netflix posted a Q1 revenue beat at $12.25 billion, though EPS was inflated by a $2.8 billion Warner Bros. Discovery termination fee and shares still dropped on a softer Q2 setup. The board added a $25 billion buyback on April 22 and then executed a record $4.7 billion of repurchases in Q2, while the July 16 print only in-lined $12.56 billion of revenue and tightened full-year sales to $51.0–$51.4 billion. Legal risk built from May 11 through September 28 as Texas and Florida attorneys general plus an Ohio class action targeted ads, kids’ data, and alleged dark patterns. Into October 8 the Street is split: Wells Fargo, HSBC, Barclays, and Goldman cut ratings or targets on engagement, Deutsche Bank and Guggenheim stayed buyers, and Disney licensing plus exclusive WWE Japan added only modest content support.
dossiers.key_assumption: The October 20 Q3 print does not cut the $51.0–$51.4 billion revenue or 31.5% margin targets, and the state AG/privacy cases stay filing-stage costs rather than a structural hit to the ads and data model.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: On July 27, 2026 Noble reported a $37 million Q2 net loss after a $43 million Brazil-rig suspension, cut 2026 adjusted EBITDA guidance to $850–$925 million, and the shares fell 9.07% to $39.20 on July 28. Management refinanced $795 million of 8.0–8.5% 2030 notes with $800 million of 6.25% 2034s on June 11, Fearnley upgraded to Buy on July 29, and Citi lifted its target to $50 on September 7, even as J.P. Morgan cut its target to $40 on October 3. Middle East tensions and a surge in oil prices lifted Noble about 7% with other offshore drillers on October 8, leaving the 2026 earnings reset only partly offset by backlog adds and a late tape bounce.
dossiers.key_assumption: The Brazil suspensions and July EBITDA cut define the 2026 earnings path, and neither the Ghana/backlog wins nor the October oil/geopolitical bounce restore pre-cut utilization or guidance.

dossiers.catalyst_stack: Transocean stacked multi-year backlog through 2026, capped by the June 30 Equinor package of more than $1 billion across seven rig-years, after the April 14 Petrobras Corcovado extension, June 16 Norge/Equinox awards, August 20 ONGC KG2 letter of award, and the October 8 Conqueror Equatorial Guinea add. U.S. merger gates cleared with CFIUS approval on June 29 and DOJ/HSR antitrust clearance on September 30 for the $5.8 billion Valaris all-stock deal, and a September 24 SDNY ruling dismissed the idle-rig securities class action without prejudice. Operations printed a May 4 Q1 revenue beat to $1.08 billion and an August 5 Q2 EPS beat to $0.03, while Barclays (May 7), Fearnley (August 7), and Zacks (October 7) upgraded the stock against a short float still above 20%. The May 4 DOJ Second Request was the principal negative catalyst and has been overtaken by the September 30 clearance.
dossiers.key_assumption: Remaining Valaris closing conditions (especially Brazil CADE) are satisfied and the Equinor/Petrobras/ONGC backlog converts at contracted dayrates without an oil-price FID stall.
